### FINDING_13: **correctness** `python/review_pipeline.py:364-366` — Plan-mode `finding_reviewers` attribution regressed in round-1 feedback: tokenization changed from `re.split(r"[,\s]+", …)` to `cell.split(",")` only. That preserves labels with internal spaces (e.g. `Cursor-dyn-Api Contract`), but breaks the tally contract for multi-reviewer cells that are whitespace-separated. `plan_review_tally._sanitize_tsv_cell` turns tab separators into spaces, and `skills/design/scripts/test-findings-classification.sh` pins `finding_reviewers` to `Cursor-Pragmatic Codex-Arch` for a tab-separated ballot line. With comma-only splitting, that whole string is one token, so neither `Cursor-Pragmatic` nor `Codex-Arch` gets credited in the prune ledger. Affected reviewers can show `0/0/0` despite real accepts/rejects, which skews net score and the 1/3 acceptance floor (false prune or false keep). Aggregator-merged findings usually use commas, so this mainly hits pre-merge / whitespace-separated cells. **Suggested fix:** In plan mode, tokenize with label-map-aware logic: if the cell is an exact label-map value, treat it as one token; if it contains commas, split on commas; otherwise fall back to whitespace splitting (or longest-match against known label values). Add a regression test mirroring the tally fixture (`Cursor-Pragmatic Codex-Arch`) and keep `test_reviewer_prune_record_plan_mode_preserves_spaced_dynamic_label`.

## risk-integration: python/review_pipeline.py:455-481

[latent] _ledger_history aborts the entire prune filter on the first malformed ledger row via bare int() parsing. A single corrupt count or round field in an otherwise valid ledger causes reviewer_prune_filter to fail-open and retain the full panel for all combos in rounds 3-4. Skip or isolate malformed rows with a diagnostic instead of failing the whole history read.

## risk-integration: python/test_review_pipeline.py

[nit] No pytest covers old-schema or corrupt-ledger fail-open despite acceptance criteria. A 5-column ledger or bad rejected_count could regress to hard failure or silent mis-pruning without CI signal. Add a filter test asserting PRUNE_FAIL_OPEN=true and an unpruned manifest when the ledger schema is invalid.

## architecture: python/review_pipeline.py:574-588

[nit] ensure_reviewer_prune_ledger has no in-repo Python callers. Header repair and new-schema row filtering are untested in live design/implement paths that may still use embedded shell helpers. Wire the helper at ledger init or remove it if obsolete.

## correctness: python/review_pipeline.py:2092-2108

[nit] aggregator-validation-exhausted records classification but not prune-ledger history. A combo with two poor settled rounds plus one aggregator-exhausted round may not be pruned until round 4 instead of round 3. Document as intentional or record a zero-yield ledger row when classification was written.

## risk-integration: python/test_review_pipeline.py

[nit] No pytest asserts PRUNE_FAIL_OPEN on old 5-column ledger despite acceptance criteria and docs/linting.md claim. A future regression in _ledger_history column checks could stop fail-open silently while CI still passes make test-reviewer-prune. Add filter test with legacy header/rows expecting PRUNE_FAIL_OPEN=true and full manifest preserved.

## risk-integration: python/review_pipeline.py:574-588

[nit] ensure_reviewer_prune_ledger 7-column rewrite has no callers or unit tests. Header repair behavior can drift without signal until/unless the helper is wired. Add focused unit test or wire a caller if repair is still intended.
